title: Fusion 360 .cps Post Processor + HTTP API Bridge
description: Build the Fusion 360 .cps post processor that serves as PRISM's primary CAM integration point. The .cps file collects all context from Fusion's post processor API (operations, tools, stock, machine, WCS) and communicates with the PRISM server via HTTP for real-time optimization (Phase A), or exports enriched G-code with sidecar JSON for offline processing (Phase B fallback). Build the HTTP API endpoint on the PRISM server side. Create the Fusion properties panel with full PRISM configuration options.

phases.title: PRISM HTTP API for Post Processing

units.title: HTTP API endpoint: POST /api/post-process — accepts job context, returns optimized G-code
steps: Create HTTP server endpoint in PRISM MCP server (Express/Fastify route)
POST /api/post-process — main optimization endpoint
Request body: { machine, controller, tools[], operations[], stock, material, coolant, aggressiveness, enabled_stages[], output_format }
Each operation includes: type, tool_number, toolpath_blocks[], depths, tolerances, surface_finish_target
Response: { gcode: string, analytics: AnalyticsReport, setup_sheet: SetupSheet, warnings: Warning[], cycle_time: CycleTimeEstimate }
GET /api/post-process/machines — list available machines from catalog
GET /api/post-process/materials — list available materials from DB
GET /api/post-process/tools — search tool catalog
GET /api/post-process/controllers — list supported controller dialects
GET /api/post-process/health — health check + version
POST /api/post-process/resolve — resolve machine/tool/material without running pipeline (for UI preview)
Response includes timing data and stage-by-stage trace for debugging
CORS headers for local development (localhost origins)
Error handling: validation errors (400), engine errors (500), timeout (504)
exit_conditions: POST /api/post-process accepts job and returns optimized G-code
Response time < 5 seconds for typical 3-operation program
Catalog query endpoints return searchable results
Error responses include actionable error messages

units.title: Fusion 360 PRISM.cps — Context extraction + PRISM server communication
steps: Create PRISM.cps post processor file (JavaScript for Fusion 360 HSM post engine)
Post processor description and legal headers
Implement onOpen(): initialize state, check PRISM server connectivity
Implement onSection(): capture per-operation context:
Tool data: type, diameter, flute_count, corner_radius, length, holder_description
Operation: type (2D pocket, 3D contour, drilling, etc.), strategy, tolerance, stock_to_leave
Cutting parameters: user-set speed/feed (as baseline), depths (ap, ae as configured in CAM)
WCS: work offset number, origin, orientation
Stock: remaining stock model (bounding box at minimum)
Implement onLinear()/onCircular()/onRapid(): build toolpath block list with coordinates
Implement onSectionEnd(): package section data
Implement onClose(): send complete job to PRISM server, receive optimized G-code, write output
Phase A (server mode): HTTP POST to localhost:PORT/api/post-process
Send: all operations, tools, machine, material as JSON
Receive: optimized G-code → write to output file
Phase B (offline mode): if server unreachable, fall back to standard post processing
Generate standard G-code using Fusion's built-in post engine
Export sidecar JSON with all captured context for later PRISM optimization
Sidecar path: output_file.json alongside output_file.nc
exit_conditions: PRISM.cps installs in Fusion 360 post processor library
Post generates dialog with PRISM-specific properties
Phase A: server running → optimized G-code output
Phase B: server down → standard G-code + sidecar JSON
Context extraction captures all tool, operation, and stock data from Fusion API

units.title: Fusion 360 Properties Panel — Full PRISM configuration in post processor dialog
steps: Define Fusion post processor properties (shown in post processor dialog):
Group: Machine Setup
Machine model (dropdown populated from /api/post-process/machines or manual entry)
Controller type (auto-detected from machine selection or manual override)
Controller version (for feature capability matching)
Group: Optimization
Aggressiveness slider (0.0-1.0, default 0.5)
Optimization target (dropdown: balanced / max_speed / max_tool_life / min_cost)
Enable/disable toggles for each optimization phase:
☑ Chip thinning compensation
☑ Corner feed reduction
☑ Stability lobe RPM selection
☑ Wear progression tracking
☑ Thermal accumulation tracking
☑ Tool deflection compensation
☑ Controller feature injection
☑ Machine error compensation
☑ Stochastic verification
Group: Material Override
Material (dropdown or text — overrides Fusion's material if set)
Hardness (HRC/HB — overrides catalog default)
Group: Output Options
Include setup sheet (boolean, default true)
Include analytics report (boolean, default true)
Include probe routines (boolean + type selection)
Output format (G-code only / G-code + report / full package)
Group: Advanced
PRISM server URL (default: http://localhost:PORT)
Linearization tolerance (mm, default 0.01)
Confidence level for stochastic analysis (%, default 95)
Debug mode (include stage timings in comments)
Properties are persistent across Fusion sessions (stored in user preferences)
exit_conditions: All property groups visible in Fusion post processor dialog
Property values pass through to PRISM server API call
Toggle states correctly enable/disable pipeline stages
